questions.question: Under Section 21 of the Factories Act 1948, every dangerous part of any machinery must be securely protected by:

options.A: Substantial fencing or safety guards

questions.question: What is the primary function of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) on the shop floor?

options.A: To completely eliminate hazards at source
options.B: To serve as the last line of defense against occupational hazards and reduce injury severity

questions.question: Which PPE item is mandatory for preventing severe head injuries from falling objects or overhead hazards in a workshop?

options.A: Industrial Safety Helmet (Hard Hat)

questions.question: Under Factories Act 1948 (Section 35), eye protection (goggles or face shields) must be provided during which operations?

options.A: Grinding, welding, riveting, and metal chipping

questions.question: What type of footwear is mandatory on the workshop floor to prevent foot crush injuries and puncture wounds?

options.A: Canvas shoes
options.B: Industrial Safety Shoes with steel toe-cap and puncture-resistant sole

questions.question: What is 'LOTO' procedure in electrical and mechanical machine maintenance safety?

options.A: Lockout / Tagout (isolating power sources and padlocking/tagging control switches before repair work)

questions.question: What is the main purpose of placing a 'DANGER - DO NOT OPERATE' red safety tag during LOTO?

options.A: To inform other workers that maintenance is in progress and power must not be turned ON
options.B: To indicate the machine is brand new

questions.question: Under Section 22 of the Factories Act 1948, who is permitted to clean, lubricate, or adjust any part of a machine in motion?

options.A: Any worker available nearby
options.B: Only a specially trained adult male worker wearing tight-fitting clothing

questions.question: Under Section 23 of the Factories Act 1948, young persons (below 18 years) are prohibited from working on dangerous machines unless:

options.A: They have received full instruction/training and are under direct supervision of an experienced person

questions.question: On a bench grinding machine, what is the maximum permissible gap between the tool rest and the grinding wheel?

options.A: 1.5 mm (1/16 inch)

questions.question: Why is a large gap between the tool rest and grinding wheel extremely dangerous?

options.A: The workpiece can get jammed in the gap, causing wheel breakage or flying shrapnel injuries

questions.question: What safety test must be performed on a new grinding wheel to detect internal cracks before mounting?

options.A: Ring Test (tapping wheel lightly with a non-metallic mallet to listen for a clear metallic ring)

questions.question: What is the purpose of an 'Emergency Stop' (E-Stop) pushbutton on a shop machine?

options.A: To instantly disconnect power and bring the machine to a rapid halt in case of emergency

questions.question: What standard color and shape is used globally for Emergency Stop pushbuttons?

options.A: Red mushroom-head button on a yellow background

questions.question: Why is it strictly dangerous to wear loose clothing, neckties, rings, or wristwatches while operating a Lathe Machine?

options.A: They can get entangled in rotating spindles or chucks, pulling the operator into the machine

questions.question: While operating a Lathe or Drilling Machine, long hair must be:

options.A: Tied back securely or covered with a protective hairnet/cap

questions.question: What tool should always be removed from a lathe chuck before switching ON the power motor?

options.A: Chuck Key

questions.question: What happens if a Chuck Key is left inside the lathe chuck when the motor is started?

options.A: It gets thrown off violently like a high-speed missile, causing severe injury or death

questions.question: What safety device is used to safely remove hot metal swarf/chips from a lathe bed?

options.A: Metal rake / Chip hook or brush (NEVER use bare hands)
options.C: Cotton cloth held in hand while machine runs

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to clear metal chips using compressed air blowing pipes?

options.A: High-pressure air propels razor-sharp metal particles at high speed into eyes and skin of nearby workers
options.B: It cools the machine too fast

questions.question: Under Section 38 of the Factories Act 1948, every workshop must provide adequate means of escape in case of:

options.A: Fire

questions.question: Workshop emergency exit doors must open in which direction?

options.A: Outwards (in the direction of exit travel) and must NEVER be locked/fastened during working hours
options.D: They must be padlocked at all times

questions.question: What is the PASS acronym rule for operating a portable Fire Extinguisher?

options.A: Pull the pin, Aim at base of fire, Squeeze the lever, Sweep side to side
options.B: Press button, Ask help, Stop work, Run away
options.C: Pour water, Call supervisor, Shut doors, Stand back
options.D: Push lever, Activate siren, Save tools, Stop fire

questions.question: Which fire extinguisher type is specifically recommended for Electrical Fires (Class C / Energized equipment)?

options.A: Carbon Dioxide (CO2) or Dry Chemical Powder (DCP) Extinguisher

questions.question: Why should Water Extinguishers NEVER be used on energized electrical fires?

options.A: Water conducts electricity, creating a severe risk of fatal electric shock/electrocution to the operator
options.C: Water makes electrical panels rust instantly

questions.question: Class A fires involve which type of combustible materials?

options.A: Ordinary solid combustibles like wood, paper, cloth, trash, and rubber
options.B: Flammable liquids like petrol, oil, grease, paint

questions.question: Class B fires involve which type of materials?

options.A: Flammable liquids (diesel, petrol, thinners, paints, oils)

questions.question: Class D fires involve which specific materials?

options.A: Combustible metals (magnesium, titanium, potassium, sodium)

questions.question: What type of extinguishing agent is required for fighting Class D metal fires?

options.A: Specialized Dry Powder (e.g., TEC / Ternary Eutectic Chloride / Sand)

questions.question: In gas welding/cutting, what safety device must be fitted in fuel and oxygen gas lines to prevent flames from traveling back into cylinders?

options.A: Flashback Arrestor (Non-return safety valve)

questions.question: In gas cylinder handling, Acetylene gas cylinders must ALWAYS be stored and operated in which orientation?

options.A: Upright / Vertical position (to prevent liquid acetone from escaping)

questions.question: What is the standard color code used for Acetylene Gas Cylinders in Indian Railways?

options.A: Maroon

questions.question: What is the standard color code for Oxygen Gas Cylinders in Indian Railways?

options.A: Black

questions.question: Why must oil or grease NEVER come in contact with Oxygen cylinder valves and regulators?

options.A: High-pressure oxygen reacts violently with oil/grease, causing spontaneous combustion or severe explosion

questions.question: In electric arc welding, what shade filter lens is worn in welding helmets to protect eyes from infrared and ultraviolet radiation (Arc Eye)?

options.A: Shade 10 to 14 welding filter glass

questions.question: What safety equipment protects nearby shop workers from arc glare radiation generated during electric welding?

options.A: Portable Welding Screens / Protective Fire-resistant Curtains

questions.question: Under Section 28 & 29 of the Factories Act 1948, all lifting machinery (cranes, hoists, chains, slings) must be thoroughly examined by a Competent Person at least once every:

options.A: 12 months (1 year)

questions.question: What does 'SWL' stamped on lifting chains, wire ropes, and EOT cranes stand for?

options.A: Safe Working Load

questions.question: What happens if an EOT Crane attempts to lift a load exceeding its rated SWL?

options.A: Risk of structural crane failure, cable snapping, or tipping, causing catastrophic accidents

questions.question: What safety limit switch is provided on an EOT Crane hoist to prevent the hook block from colliding with the overhead drum?

options.A: Over-hoist Limit Switch (Upper Limit Switch)

questions.question: When guiding suspended heavy loads moved by EOT Cranes, riggers should use:

options.A: Tag lines (guide ropes) to control load rotation from a safe distance
options.B: Bare hands directly pushing the swinging weight
options.C: Iron rods jammed under the load

questions.question: Standing or walking under a suspended overhead crane load is:

options.A: Strictly prohibited at all times

questions.question: What safety device is fitted on a crane hook to prevent wire rope slings from slipping out accidentally?

options.A: Safety Latch (Hook Latch)

questions.question: According to general safety standards, Full Body Safety Harness must be worn when working at heights above:

options.A: 1.8 meters (6 feet)

questions.question: Where should the lanyard snap hook of a Full Body Safety Harness be anchored when working at height?

options.A: To a rigid overhead anchor point or tested lifeline capable of supporting high impact load
options.D: To a light electrical conduit pipe

questions.question: What safety rule applies to portable extension ladders on the shop floor?

options.A: Set ladder at a 4:1 slope angle (75 degrees) with anti-slip feet and extend 1 meter above landing platform
options.C: Place ladder on greasy oil drums

questions.question: What is 'Three-Point Contact' rule when climbing up or down ladders or crane cabins?

options.A: Maintaining contact with two hands and one foot, or two feet and one hand at all times
options.B: Having three workers on the ladder
options.C: Climbing with hands free holding tools
options.D: Jumping down three steps at a time

questions.question: Under Indian Electricity Rules, what minimum insulation mat specification is required in front of high voltage switchboards?

options.A: BIS approved Electrical Rubber Insulating Mats (IS 15652 standard)

questions.question: What is the primary function of Equipment Earthing (Grounding) in shop machinery?

options.A: To safely divert leakage current directly to ground, tripping circuit breakers and preventing electric shock to operators
options.B: To supply operating voltage to motor
options.D: To prevent rust on machine legs

questions.question: What safety device automatically disconnects power supply instantly upon detecting a small earth leakage current (e.g., 30mA)?

options.A: ELCB (Earth Leakage Circuit Breaker) / RCCB (Residual Current Circuit Breaker)

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to replace a blown electrical fuse wire with a thick copper wire?

options.A: Thick wire will not melt during overload, causing electrical cable fires and motor destruction

questions.question: What is 'Permit to Work' (PTW) in shop floor maintenance?

options.A: Formal written document confirming isolation of energy sources, atmospheric testing, and safety clearances before high-risk work begins
options.C: Gate pass for leaving workshop early

questions.question: Before entering a Confined Space (e.g., fuel tank, boiler drum, deep pit), what mandatory test must be conducted?

options.A: Gas testing for Oxygen level (19.5-23.5%), toxic gases, and explosive vapor concentrations using a gas detector

questions.question: What safety equipment must be provided to workers entering a oxygen-deficient or toxic gas confined space?

options.A: Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA) or Supplied-Air Respirator

questions.question: Under 5S Housekeeping methodology, what does the first 'S' (SEIRI / Sort) signify?

options.A: Separating necessary items from unnecessary items and removing clutter from the shop floor

questions.question: Why is good housekeeping (5S) directly related to shop floor safety?

options.A: It eliminates slip, trip, and fall hazards, keeps walkways clear, and reduces fire risks from oily rags/debris
options.D: It eliminates the need for supervisors

questions.question: Yellow safety lines painted on the workshop floor designate:

options.A: Clear gangways / walkways for pedestrian movement and material transport routes that must NEVER be obstructed
options.B: Areas reserved for parking personal bikes

questions.question: How should oil or chemical spills on the shop floor be treated immediately?

options.A: Cleaned up instantly using oil-absorbent granules, sawdust, or spill kits, and marked with warning cones
options.B: Left to dry naturally in air
options.D: Washed into storm water drains with water

questions.question: What is 'MSDS' or 'SDS' that must be available for all chemicals used on the shop floor?

options.A: Material Safety Data Sheet (Safety Data Sheet detailing chemical properties, health risks, PPE, and first-aid instructions)

questions.question: In case of chemical splash into a worker's eyes, what immediate first-aid action must be taken?

options.A: Flush eyes continuously with clean running water at Emergency Eye Wash Station for at least 15 minutes and seek medical aid
options.B: Rub eyes vigorously with dirty cloth

questions.question: What safety rule applies to compressed air usage on the shop floor?

options.A: NEVER point compressed air nozzles at oneself or others, and NEVER use compressed air to blow dust off clothes or skin
options.B: Use high pressure air to dry wet hair
options.C: Use compressed air to clean dusty faces
options.D: Blow compressed air into ears to clear dust

questions.question: What serious medical condition can occur if high-pressure compressed air penetrates skin or open wounds?

options.A: Air Embolism (air bubbles in bloodstream), which can cause fatal stroke or heart failure

questions.question: Under Section 31 of Factories Act 1948, Air Reservoirs (Pressure Vessels) must be fitted with which vital safety device?

options.A: Safety Relief Valve (Pop Safety Valve) and pressure gauge

questions.question: What happens if a pressure vessel safety relief valve is jammed shut or mechanically locked by an operator?

options.A: Pressure can rise uncontrollably beyond bursting threshold, resulting in a catastrophic vessel explosion

questions.question: What type of machine guard uses light beams / photoelectric curtains to stop machine movement when a worker's hand enters the dangerous zone?

options.A: Photoelectric Safety Light Curtain (Presence-sensing Guard)

questions.question: What is an 'Interlocked Machine Guard'?

options.A: A guard connected to power controls such that machine cannot operate unless guard is closed, and opening guard stops machine
options.B: A guard locked with a padlock permanently

questions.question: Why is removing or bypassing machine safety guards strictly considered a serious disciplinary offense?

options.A: Exposes operators to nip points, rotating shafts, or crushing zones, leading to severe amputations or fatal accidents

questions.question: What is 'In-running Nip Point' on mechanical drives?

options.A: Dangerous zone where rotating parts move towards each other or past a fixed component (e.g., gears, belts/pulleys, chain/sprockets)
options.C: Point where electric plug is connected

questions.question: All belt-pulley drives, gear trains, and coupling shafts on shop machinery must be protected by:

options.A: Complete Enclosure Guards / Fixed Mesh Guards
options.B: Yellow paint lines on floor only

questions.question: While operating a Hydraulic Power Press, what dual-control safety system ensures operator hands remain outside the die crushing zone?

options.A: Two-Hand Control System (requires pressing two buttons simultaneously with both hands to actuate stroke)

questions.question: What safety precautions must be taken before working inside a Hydraulic Press die area during tool setup?

options.A: Insert mechanical Safety Blocks / Die Props, depressurize hydraulics, and apply LOTO

questions.question: Under Factories Act 1948 (Section 34), maximum permissible weight limit for manual lifting by adult male workers is governed by rules. What is the standard safe manual lifting limit per person without mechanical aid?

options.A: 50 kg (or as specified in state factory rules, typically 50 kg for adult males, 30 kg for adult females)

questions.question: What is the correct ergonomic posture for lifting a heavy load manually from the shop floor?

options.A: Keep back straight, bend knees/legs, hold load close to body, and lift using leg muscles
options.B: Keep legs straight and bend waist forward completely
options.C: Twist spine while lifting heavy load rapidly
options.D: Lift load holding it at arm's length away from body

questions.question: What hazard is created by leaving greasy cotton rags lying near electrical panels or hot steam pipes?

options.A: Spontaneous Combustion / Severe fire outbreak risk

questions.question: Greasy and oily cotton waste rags must be disposed of in:

options.A: Self-closing metal fire-resistant waste bins marked for oily waste

questions.question: When operating wood-working machinery (e.g., circular saw, band saw), what safety device prevents hands from contacting saw blade?

options.A: Push Stick / Push Block and adjustable blade guards
options.D: Using bare palms close to blade

questions.question: Why is wearing loose cotton gloves near rotating drilling spindles or milling cutters extremely dangerous?

options.A: Glove fabric can catch on the rotating tool, rapidly dragging the hand and fingers into the cutter
options.C: Gloves cool down the drill bit

questions.question: What safety equipment protects shop floor technicians from high noise levels (> 85 dBA) generated by heavy forging hammers or pneumatic chippers?

options.A: Ear Muffs or Ear Plugs (Hearing Protection)

questions.question: Continuous unallocated exposure to industrial noise above 85 dBA for 8 hours daily causes:

options.A: Noise-Induced Hearing Loss (NIHL) - permanent irreversible hearing damage

questions.question: In a Battery Charging Room, what gas is released during battery charging that poses a severe fire/explosion hazard?

options.A: Hydrogen gas (highly explosive in air concentrations above 4%)

questions.question: What mandatory safety systems must be functional in a Metro rake Battery Charging Room?

options.A: Flameproof electrical fittings, continuous forced exhaust ventilation, and 'NO SMOKING / NO OPEN FLAME' signs

questions.question: In electric arc welding, the welding machine's return current clamp (Earth Clamp) should be attached:

options.A: Directly to the workpiece as close as possible to the welding spot to prevent stray currents
options.B: To a water pipe 50 meters away
options.C: To building steel structure miles away

questions.question: What is 'Stray Current Hazard' in arc welding?

options.A: Welding current returning through crane wire ropes, bearing races, or building steelwork, causing arcing and catastrophic damage
options.C: Current turning into heat in electrode

questions.question: What safety rule applies when replacing fluorescent light tubes or working near high ceilings in workshop bays?

options.A: Use certified Mobile Elevating Work Platforms (MEWP / Scissor Lift) or properly secured scaffolding with safety harness
options.B: Stand on top of a moving crane hook
options.C: Balance on wooden boxes stacked on forklift forks
options.D: Climb up bare electrical conduit pipes

questions.question: Forklift trucks operating inside workshop bays must be equipped with which mandatory safety features?

options.A: Flashing amber beacon light, reverse backup alarm, horn, overhead operator guard (FOPS), and seatbelt

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit generally permitted for forklift trucks and material handling vehicles inside workshop aisles?

options.A: 5 to 10 km/h

questions.question: When driving a loaded Forklift, if the load blocks the driver's forward view, the driver must:

options.A: Drive the forklift in REVERSE safely (or use a spotter guide)
options.B: Drive forward blindly sounding horn continuously
options.C: Speed up to finish travel quickly

questions.question: What safety check must be performed on pneumatic tools (e.g., air grinders, impact wrenches) before connecting to air line?

options.A: Check air hose for cracks/damage, ensure safety whip-checks are installed on couplings, and check rated tool speed

questions.question: What is a 'Whip-Check Safety Cable' on pneumatic hose lines?

options.A: Steel wire cable bridging hose couplings to prevent violent whipping of hose if coupling breaks under pressure

questions.question: Under Factories Act 1948, what is 'Safety Committee' composition in a workshop employing 250 or more workers?

options.A: Equal representation of management officers and worker representatives to review safety matters monthly

questions.question: Who is appointed as 'Safety Officer' in a workshop under Section 40B of the Factories Act 1948?

options.A: Mandatory qualified Safety Officer appointed in factories ordinarily employing 1000 or more workers (or hazardous processes)

questions.question: What is 'Near Miss' incident in workshop safety terminology?

options.A: An unplanned event that did not result in injury or damage this time, but had potential to do so if conditions differed slightly

questions.question: Why is reporting and investigating 'Near Misses' crucial on the shop floor?

options.A: Identifies root hazards and enables preventive corrective actions BEFORE an actual injury/fatality occurs

questions.question: In safety signage standard color codes, RED color signifies:

options.A: Prohibition signs (e.g., NO SMOKING) and Firefighting equipment

questions.question: BLUE color circular safety signs signify:

options.A: Mandatory Action Signs (e.g., WEAR EYE PROTECTION, WEAR SAFETY SHOES)

questions.question: YELLOW or AMBER triangular safety signs signify:

options.A: Warning / Caution Signs (e.g., RISK OF ELECTRIC SHOCK, HOT SURFACE)

questions.question: GREEN square or rectangular safety signs signify:

options.A: Safe Condition Signs (e.g., FIRST AID KIT, EMERGENCY EXIT, EYE WASH STATION)

questions.question: What safety check is conducted on synthetic web slings (nylon/polyester) before rigged lifting?

options.A: Inspect for cuts, acid burns, melted fibers, broken stitching, or missing SWL capacity tag (reject if damaged)

questions.question: Why is it strictly prohibited to heat or weld a damaged crane lifting alloy steel chain link?

options.A: Welding heat destroys the heat treatment and metallurgical strength of alloy steel, causing sudden brittle failure under load

questions.question: What is 'Toolbox Safety Talk' (TBT) conducted on the shop floor?

options.A: Short 5-10 minute safety briefing conducted by SSE/JE with workers at the start of shift regarding job hazards and controls

questions.question: What is 'Job Safety Analysis' (JSA) or 'Job Hazard Analysis' (JHA)?

options.A: Risk assessment procedure breaking a job down into steps, identifying hazards at each step, and defining control measures

questions.question: Why is strict adherence to machine and shop floor safety measures vital for a Junior Engineer (JE) in Metro Railway Kolkata?

options.A: Protects worker lives, prevents disabling accidents, ensures zero-defect maintenance, maintains high morale, and avoids legal penalties
options.B: To increase paper documentation in office
options.D: To exhaust workshop safety budget intentionally
